```{r}
m <- 25      # Total number of tests
i <- 1:m     # Rank vector (1 to 25)
i_over_m <- i / m # This is the theoretical "expected noise" line
```

```{r}
# --- Graph 1: "Noise-Only" World ---
# What do P-values look like if ALL tests are "noise" (all nulls are true)?
# By definition, they are uniformly distributed between 0 and 1.
p_values_noise <- runif(1000, min = 0, max = 1)

# Sort them from smallest to largest
p_values_noise_sorted <- sort(p_values_noise)

# Plot the sorted P-values against their rank (i)
plot(1:m, p_values_noise_sorted,
     main = "Graph 1: P-Values from 'Noise' Only",
     xlab = "Rank (i)",
     ylab = "Sorted P-Value",
     pch = 20, col = "gray",
     sub = "P-values from true nulls follow the red line")

# Add the "expected noise" line (P = i/m)
lines(1:m, (1:m)/1000, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)

legend("bottomright",
       legend = c("Observed P-Values (Noise)", "Expected Line (i/m)"),
       col = c("gray", "red"),
       lty = c(NA, 2), pch = c(20, NA), lwd = c(NA, 2))
```

```{r}
# Define the Q values and their colors
Q_vals <- c(0.20, 0.10, 0.05)
colors <- c("darkgreen", "orange", "purple")

# Calculate the three BH critical value lines
bh_line_1 <- (i / m) * Q_vals[1]
bh_line_2 <- (i / m) * Q_vals[2]
bh_line_3 <- (i / m) * Q_vals[3]

# Set up the same blank plot
plot(i, i_over_m, 
     type = "n",
     main = "Graph 2: BH Critical Value Lines (Q)",
     xlab = "Rank (i)",
     ylab = "P-Value",
     ylim = c(0, 1))

# Add the original (i/m) line
lines(i, i_over_m, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)

# Add the three BH lines
lines(i, bh_line_1, col = colors[1], lty = 1, lwd = 2)
lines(i, bh_line_2, col = colors[2], lty = 1, lwd = 2)
lines(i, bh_line_3, col = colors[3], lty = 1, lwd = 2)

# Add a grid
grid()

# Add a comprehensive legend
legend("topleft",
       legend = c("Expected Line (i/m)",
                  paste("BH Line, Q =", Q_vals[1]),
                  paste("BH Line, Q =", Q_vals[2]),
                  paste("BH Line, Q =", Q_vals[3])),
       col = c("red", colors),
       lty = c(2, 1, 1, 1),
       lwd = 2)
```

```{r}
p_values <- c(0.001, 0.008, 0.039, 0.041, 0.042, 0.060, 0.074, 0.205, 0.212, 0.216, 0.222, 0.251, 0.269, 0.275, 0.34, 0.341, 0.384, 0.569, 0.594, 0.696, 0.762, 0.94, 0.942, 0.975, 0.986)
my_p_values_sorted <- sort(p_values)
# ============================================

# Define the single Q value and its line
Q_single <- 0.25
bh_line_single <- (i / m) * Q_single

# Plot your p-values as points
plot(i, my_p_values_sorted,
     pch = 20, # pch=20 gives solid circles
     col = "blue",
     main = paste("Graph 3: Finding the Cutoff (Q = 0.25)"),
     xlab = "Rank (i)",
     ylab = "Sorted P-Value",
     ylim = c(0, 1))

# Add the single BH line
lines(i, bh_line_single, 
      col = "darkgreen", 
      lty = 1, 
      lwd = 2)

# Optional: Find and draw the cutoff
# This code finds the last p-value under the line and draws crosshairs
under_line <- my_p_values_sorted <= bh_line_single
if (any(under_line)) {
  cutoff_rank <- max(which(under_line))
  cutoff_p <- my_p_values_sorted[cutoff_rank]
  
  # Add dotted lines for the cutoff
  abline(v = cutoff_rank, col = "gray", lty = 3, lwd = 2)
  abline(h = cutoff_p, col = "gray", lty = 3, lwd = 2)
  
  # Label the cutoff
  text(cutoff_rank - 0.5, 0.5, 
       paste("Cutoff Rank (k) =", cutoff_rank), 
       adj = 1, srt = 90) # srt=90 rotates text
}

# Add a grid
grid()

# Add legend
legend("topleft",
       legend = c("My P-Values",
                  paste("BH Line, Q =", Q_single)),
       col = c("blue", "darkgreen"),
       pch = c(20, NA), # Point for p-values, no point for line
       lty = c(NA, 1),  # No line for p-values, line for BH
       lwd = 2)
```
